title: Recognizing a complex exponential signal
description: read $z(t)=Ae^{j(\omega_0 t+\phi)}$ as a signal with magnitude, angular frequency, and phase.

title: Converting a complex exponential to rectangular form
description: expand the signal into explicit real and imaginary pieces.

title: Extracting the real and imaginary waveforms
description: identify the cosine waveform as the real part and the sine waveform as the imaginary part.

title: Interpreting a complex exponential in the complex plane
description: view the signal as a complex quantity with magnitude and angle that change meaningfully over time.

title: Reading phasors at $t=0$
description: interpret $z(0)=Ae^{j\phi}$ as the initial phasor with starting angle $\phi$.

title: Interpreting angular frequency as rotation rate
description: connect $\omega_0$ to how fast the phasor turns in the complex plane.

title: Real-axis projection of a phasor
description: understand the cosine component as the projection of the rotating phasor onto the real axis.

title: Imaginary-axis projection of a phasor
description: understand the sine component as the projection of the rotating phasor onto the imaginary axis.

title: Reading projection values at special angles
description: determine when the real or imaginary component becomes zero or reaches an extreme from the total angle.

title: Connecting phasor motion to time-domain sinusoids
description: understand why a rotating phasor traces sine and cosine waves over time.

title: Using complex exponentials as compact sinusoid representations
description: treat exponential form as a cleaner representation for analysis and later signal-processing work.

title: Reading sinusoid parameters
description: identify amplitude, angular frequency, and phase in expressions like $A\cos(\omega t+\phi)$ or $A\sin(\omega t+\phi)$.

title: Interpreting radians and standard angles
description: interpret angles like $\pi/2$ and $\pi$ as positions in a rotation.

title: Identifying real and imaginary parts
description: distinguish the real component of a complex number from its imaginary component.

title: Interpreting a complex number in the plane
description: view a complex number as a point or vector on the real and imaginary axes.

title: Describing magnitude and angle
description: describe a complex number by its length and direction.

title: Applying Euler's formula to exponentials
description: rewrite exponential form as cosine plus $j$ sine, and move between the two forms.
